A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe NoLiMa and contain matching main sections, Tables 1–9, Figures 1–5, and Appendices A–D. Text and visual inspection support reliable comparison despite page reflow.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations of 12 LLMs, reasoning-model experiments, and analyses of needle placement, prompting, and literal matching in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical evaluations and analyses, including the results in Tables 3–6 and Figures 2, 3, and 5.

M1.justification: Needle construction, associative-hop and inverted templates, the Contriever/Llama filtering pipeline, and prompting procedures remain unchanged in Section 3 and the appendices.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 58 question–needle pairs, book-based haystacks, NoLiMa-Hard subset, and direct-question, multiple-choice, and distractor scenarios. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The benchmark comparators in Table 1, 12 models in Table 3, and prompting/reasoning-model comparisons in Tables 4–6 retain identical membership. The newly cited Michelangelo work is not evaluated.

E3.justification: The context lengths, 7,540-test main evaluation design, needle-placement procedures, scoring thresholds, model revisions, decoding budgets, and distractor-placement rules are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices B–D.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 retains the same hop/inversion, aligned-depth, CoT, reasoning-model, literal-match, and distractor analyses. Moving Figure 3 does not add or revise an analysis.

E5.justification: Aggregation over five haystacks and the placement/smoothing descriptions are unchanged. Neither version reports seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Reported numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged. For example, Table 3 gives GPT-4o a 99.3 base score and 69.7 at 32K in both versions; Tables 4–6 also retain their results.

T1.justification: The definitions of base score, normalized score, and effective length in Section 4.3 are unchanged. Neither version adds or removes formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The benchmark contribution and central claims about literal matching, long-context degradation, and the limited benefits of CoT/reasoning models remain unchanged. The added abstract sentence supplies resource-access information.

C2.justification: Interpretations involving causal attention, needle order, positional effects, and distractors are retained. The mechanistic-analysis qualification in Section 4.4.1 and downstream/RAG discussion in Section 5 are also unchanged.

D1.justification: The v2 abstract adds a public-release statement and a GitHub link for the dataset and evaluation code, absent from v1. Technical details in Appendices A–D remain unchanged; the PDFs establish the added access disclosure.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Vodrahalli et al. (2024), Michelangelo: Long context evaluations beyond haystacks via latent structure queries, with a corresponding reference entry. The existing research-positioning argument is unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract gains one resource-release sentence, related work gains one citation and reference entry, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. Existing exposition, terminology, and section order are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 3 moves from the bottom of page 6 to the top of page 7, accompanied by text and bibliography reflow. Figure graphics, table structures, and captions are unchanged; the appendix pages are visually identical.

improvement.justification: The new dataset/code release statement and repository link improve resource discoverability and reproducibility documentation, while the Michelangelo citation modestly improves related-work coverage. The scientific evidence and appendices remain unchanged, so the supported overall benefit is limited.
